q: How much does it cost?
k: price fee fees cost money pay payment charge expensive cheap per week match fee invoice bank transfer cash entry free
a:
Entry is free. The match fee is £30 a team each week (about £3.75 a player in a squad of 8).
Fees for the 10-week season are invoiced at the start and paid weekly by bank transfer, at least 24 hours before each match night. Cash isn't accepted on the night (rules 2.2 and 2.3).

q: How do I enter a team?
k: join enter register sign up signup new team start apply application form entry how mates mate friends friend group
a:
Fill in the online registration form on the Join a league page: /join.html
The captain must be 18 or over, and every team needs at least 6 registered players, including the captain, before its first fixture (rules 1.1 and 1.4).

q: What nights and times are the games?
k: when time times kick off kickoff kick-off start night nights day days monday thursday evening schedule hours what time
a:
- Monday League: 7pm – 10pm, kick-offs 19:00, 19:35, 20:10, 20:45 and 21:20
- Thursday League: 7pm – 9.40pm, kick-offs 19:00, 19:40, 20:20 and 21:00
Your team's fixtures are on the League page: /league.html

q: Where is it played?
k: where venue address location pitch ground directions find postcode map academy hereford 3g site dog dogs smoking smoke vaping vape speed limit
a:
All games are on the floodlit 3G pitch at The Hereford Church of England Academy, Marlbrook Road, Hereford, HR2 7NG.
Directions and the site rules (10mph speed limit, no dogs, no smoking or vaping) are on the Venue page: /venue.html

q: What boots can I wear?
k: boots boot footwear shoes trainers studs moulds moulded screw blades astro astros wear feet shin pads shinpads
a:
- Moulded studs or screw-in studs: fine
- Astro trainers: only as a last resort if you have no suitable boots
- Bladed (chevron) studs and flat-soled trainers: not allowed on the 3G pitch
Shin pads are compulsory (rules 5.23 and 5.24). More on the Venue page: /venue.html

q: How long are the games?
k: long length duration minutes halves half time each way how long match length game length
a: Monday games are 16 minutes each way and Thursday games are 18 minutes each way, with no more than 1 minute at half time (rule 5.2).

q: How many players and substitutes?
k: players squad size team size how many substitutes subs bench rolling six a side 6-a-side side
a: It's six a side, including the goalkeeper, plus up to three substitutes with unlimited rolling substitutions. Your squad can be any size, but every player must be registered (rules 5.1 and 5.19).

q: How old do you have to be?
k: age old minimum young under 16 18 adult adults kids children junior juniors teenager
a: Players must be 16 or over, and the team captain must be 18 or over (rules 1.1 and 1.3).

q: Can I play if I don't have a team?
k: individual single player myself alone on my own no team without team looking for team free agent solo drop in turn up
a: Super 6s is for teams. If you just want a game, try Drop In & Play: Sundays 7pm – 8pm at the Herefordshire FA 3G pitch, £4, no team needed. More sessions are on the Get involved page: /get-involved.html

q: How do we add new players?
k: add player new player register player registration sign player mid season change squad name address date of birth
a: New players can join at any time in the season. Email their full name, home address and date of birth to Super6s@HerefordshireFA.com, or give them to the Event Manager, before they play (rule 1.3).

q: Can I play for two teams?
k: two teams second team another team both teams play for more than one team move transfer switch change team
a: Yes: a player can play for up to two teams on the same night, as long as they're in different divisions. To move teams, you leave your current team and register with the new one (rules 1.5 and 1.6).

q: What if we can't make a game?
k: can't make cant make cannot absence absent miss missing away holiday skip week unavailable postpone call off notice
a: Each team can give notice of one absence per season. The captain must email Super6s@HerefordshireFA.com before 12 noon on match day and pay the match fee less a £10 discount. Without notice, the other team is awarded a 5–0 walkover (rule 4.1).

q: What if we're late or short of players?
k: late running late delayed short players not enough players missing players borrow player forfeit only enough four five 4 5
a: A team more than 5 minutes late, or without enough players, forfeits the match and still pays the match fee (rule 4.4). If you're short, you can borrow a player registered to another team, with the agreement of the Event Manager and the other team (rule 1.7).

q: When does the fee have to be paid?
k: deadline pay by when pay late payment unpaid not paid owe owed debt walkover noon forget forgot
a: Pay at least 24 hours before each match night. If the full fee hasn't arrived by 12 noon on match day, the match may be awarded to the other team as a 5–0 walkover (rules 2.2 and 2.4).

q: How do we leave the league?
k: leave leaving quit stop withdraw pull out finish end notice refund credit
a: Give at least two weeks' notice by email to Super6s@HerefordshireFA.com, play your next two fixtures and clear anything owed. Teams that leave this way are refunded any credit. Leaving without notice means a £60 fine (rules 8.2, 8.4 and 2.7).

q: How long is a season?
k: season seasons weeks how long next season new season start date break summer
a: Seasons run for 10 weeks. The next season starts the week after one ends, and teams are entered automatically unless the captain gives notice (rules 3.1, 3.6 and 8.1).

q: How do points and promotion work?
k: points promotion promoted relegation relegated table league table divisions division goal difference
a: Win 3 points, draw 1, lose 0. Teams level on points are split by goal difference, then goals scored. At the end of each season the top two in each division go up and the bottom two go down (rules 3.2 and 3.3). Tables are on /league.html

q: Are there prizes?
k: prize prizes trophy trophies win winners winning champions reward medal
a: Yes: every division winner gets a trophy to keep (rule 3.4).

q: Who referees the games?
k: referee referees ref refs official officials qualified
a: Games are refereed by FA-qualified referees wherever possible. If a qualified referee can't be appointed, another person may officiate (rule 7.5).

q: What are the main playing rules?
k: rules rule laws offside slide sliding tackle tackles kick in kick-ins corner penalty penalties goal area playing
a:
A few that catch people out:
- No offside (5.9)
- No sliding or charging tackles (5.13)
- Kick-ins instead of throw-ins: side-foot, below knee height (5.7)
- Opponents 5 yards back at kick-ins, corners and free kicks (5.9)
The full rules are here: /rules.html

q: What are the goalkeeper rules?
k: goalkeeper keeper goalie gk throw throws back pass goal kick hands
a:
- The keeper may leave the area but is then an outfield player (5.14)
- Throws must be underarm, below knee height (5.15)
- Goal kicks are kicked, never thrown (5.16)
- After passing to a teammate, another player must touch the ball before it goes back to the keeper's hands (5.17)

q: What happens with yellow and red cards?
k: yellow red card cards sin bin sinbin sent off sending off ban banned suspension suspended discipline booking
a: A yellow card means 5 minutes in the sin bin; two yellows make a red. A red card means no further part in the match and a suspension of at least one league match (rules 6.2 and 6.3).

q: What kit do we need?
k: kit shirts shirt tops colours colour bibs bib matching shin pads uniform clothing away clash same colour
a: Teams wear matching coloured tops, and shin pads are compulsory. If both teams' tops are the same colour, the away team wears bibs (rules 5.25, 5.23 and 5.5).

q: Are we insured?
k: insurance insured injury injured cover covered accident
a: The league doesn't provide personal injury or player-to-player insurance, so teams and players are advised to arrange their own. Herefordshire County FA (01432 342179) can advise on providers (rule 8.6).

q: Where are the fixtures, results and tables?
k: fixtures fixture results result tables table scores score standings who are we playing next game opponents
a: Everything is on the League page: /league.html. Use "Find your team" to see your own fixtures and results. Fixtures are published at least 48 hours before the first match of the season (rule 3.5).

q: Who runs the league and how do I contact them?
k: contact manager league manager organiser organizer phone number call ring email who runs speak person
a: The league manager is Martin Oliver: 07940 241587. You can also email Super6s@HerefordshireFA.com

q: Is there support if I'm struggling?
k: mental health struggling stress stressed depressed depression anxiety anxious talk help support wellbeing suicide crisis
a: It's okay to talk. If you or someone else is in danger right now, call 999. Free, confidential support services are listed on our Wellbeing page: /wellbeing.html
